channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: Sarvam AI launches Token Factory hosting mostly Chinese models on Indian GPUs, reigniting sovereign AI debate
item.description: Sarvam AI launched Token Factory on November 16, an inference platform serving eight open-weight models through a single OpenAI-compatible API on GPU clusters in India. Six of the eight models are from Chinese companies, while Sarvam received a ₹98.68 crore government GPU subsidy to build indigenous foundation models. The launch highlights tension between India's sovereign AI ambitions and commercial pressure to host the world's best open models on local infrastructure.

item.title: Anthropic IPO set to deliver windfall to smaller VC firms
item.description: Anthropic's upcoming IPO is poised to generate multibillion-dollar returns for venture firms and tech companies that backed the Claude maker, with smaller firms like Spark Capital and Iconiq set for outsized gains. Iconiq's stake is worth about $17 billion at the company's $965 billion private valuation, and Spark Capital's $75 million investment is now worth $7 billion. The IPO will redraw VC power rankings, giving lesser-known firms returns that could surpass larger blue-chip rivals and reshaping the venture capital landscape.

item.title: LanceDB raises $57.5M Series B to expand multimodal AI lakehouse
item.description: LanceDB raised $57.5 million in Series B funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors to expand its multimodal lakehouse for AI training data. The round brings total funding to $98.5 million. The funding highlights growing investor focus on data infrastructure as a bottleneck for scaling multimodal AI model training.

item.title: Nvidia expands manufacturing capacity with suppliers to meet AI demand
item.description: Nvidia announced it is expanding global manufacturing capacity with supply chain partners including Amkor, Foxconn, and TSMC to support long-term demand for its AI platforms. The multiyear initiative spans billions of dollars in investments across advanced packaging, substrates, and optical engines through 2029. This expansion addresses the manufacturing bottlenecks constraining global AI infrastructure deployment by securing long-term supply lines for Nvidia's hardware.

item.title: San Francisco AI insiders could hold $1.2 trillion in equity as Anthropic goes public
item.description: San Francisco AI startup insiders are estimated to hold $1.2 trillion in equity, led by Anthropic, which is set to go public at an expected $1.4 trillion valuation. The IPO could unlock massive paper wealth for insiders, influencing housing markets and investor sentiment in the AI sector.

item.title: Nvidia's startup stakes reach $65.5B as interim CEO signals caution
item.description: Nvidia revealed its equity stakes in private companies reached $65.5 billion, up from $22 billion in January. However, venture capitalists anticipate a pullback in startup funding following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang and a shift in tone under interim CEO Colette Kress. As one of the largest financial backers of the artificial intelligence ecosystem, any shift in Nvidia's investment strategy under new leadership directly impacts hundreds of startups and data center projects.

item.title: Nvidia ends H200 chip sales in China under acting CEO Colette Kress
item.description: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending its participation in a deal brokered by Jensen Huang and President Donald Trump that included a 25% tariff. Acting CEO Colette Kress announced the decision following new export controls restricting advanced chips from foreign data centers serving Chinese customers. This marks a major shift in Nvidia's compliance strategy and international market access following leadership changes under acting CEO Colette Kress.

item.title: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring journalism to ChatGPT
item.description: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI entered a partnership to feature Le Groupe Figaro's journalism in ChatGPT. The integration includes summaries and excerpts alongside links to original stories. This partnership expands the presence of traditional news publishing within conversational AI platforms.

item.title: Google rolls out Gemini Tasks assistant for free in six markets
item.description: Google is rolling out its agentic AI assistant Tasks, formerly known as Gemini Spark, for free in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India. Bundled with the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, the feature allows users to make calls, book appointments, compare products, and complete purchases. The release brings agentic AI capabilities—such as making phone calls and executing purchases—to hundreds of millions of users for free, shifting AI assistants from passive chat tools to active participants in daily chores.

item.title: Sarvam AI hosts six Chinese models in India, reigniting sovereign AI debate
item.description: Sarvam AI's Token Factory, launched November 16, offers eight AI models through a single OpenAI-compatible API on Indian GPU servers, but six of the eight are built by Chinese companies. The mix has reopened debate over whether a startup backed by the IndiaAI Mission should prioritise indigenous models or make the world's best models accessible in India. Sarvam's choice to host mostly Chinese models on Indian servers exposes a tension at the heart of India's AI strategy: building homegrown models versus providing local access to the strongest existing ones.

item.title: Simon Willison releases external sandboxes for coding agents
item.description: Simon Willison and AI research lab Prime Radiant released three sandbox server implementations to safely run code executed by coding agents. The tools isolate agent-executed code to prevent damage from mistakes or prompt injection attacks. It provides new methods for developers to experiment with coding agents and local models safely by separating the agent from the code execution environment.

item.title: Nvidia board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: Nvidia's board stated it does not plan to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang following his resignation. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent replacement. The decision closes the door on the former CEO's return amid ongoing federal investigations and congressional hearings involving the chipmaker.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models with benchmark gains
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API, bringing benchmark gains and lower pricing. Artificial Analysis ranks GPT-6.2 Astra second in its main index, while Epoch AI places it tied with Claude Fable 5.2 at a score of 174 on the Epoch Capabilities Index. The release shows intense competition at the frontier of language models, with OpenAI and Anthropic achieving matching capability scores while competing on cost and specialized professional tasks.

item.title: Nvidia reports Q3 revenue of $115.8B and forecasts Q4 revenue of $130B
item.description: Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-over-year, with data center revenue reaching $107.6 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress also forecasted fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion. The financial results indicate that Nvidia's AI chip sales and data center demand continue to expand rapidly following leadership changes.

item.title: Researchers find vision-language models give harmful help from scene images
item.description: Researchers led by Tongxi Wu identified a "scene-state safety vulnerability" in which vision-language models provide harmful assistance by interpreting visual events, even without an explicit harmful request. Their attack method S3TA achieved a model-average attack success rate of 71.2% across eight VLMs, exceeding the strongest baseline by 6.1 percentage points. It shows a new way to bypass VLM safety filters that relies on the model's own scene reasoning rather than on the user's text, so defenders must protect the assistance models infer from images, not just screen input content.

item.title: Researchers propose ATI, a security layer for cross-organization AI agents
item.description: Viet K. Nguyen and Mohammad I. Husain published a paper proposing the Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI), a framework-independent security architecture for verifying identity, integrity, and authorization of AI agents operating across organizations. In their simulated eight-organization federation, enabling ATI's enforcement mechanisms increased attack containment from 43% to 84% with about 174 microseconds of overhead per request. It addresses a gap in current agent frameworks—no common way to verify cross-organizational agent identity and authorization—as multi-organization agent collaboration grows.

item.title: Microsoft introduces new Copilot features and IQ platform at Ignite 2026
item.description: Microsoft announced new AI innovations at Ignite 2026, including Copilot Workspaces, Autopilot, and the Microsoft IQ enterprise context management platform. Volkswagen Group is equipping over 330,000 employees with Copilot. For those following AI, the announcements show how major technology providers are moving past basic chatbots toward persistent agents and enterprise context management systems designed for scale.

item.title: Ethan Mollick shares pre-launch experience with GPT-6.2 Astra
item.description: Ethan Mollick reported that pre-launch testing of GPT-6.2 Astra showed the model was uneven and hard to steer. However, he noted it successfully delivered an ambitious project to build a space elevator from scratch. It provides an early independent perspective on the practical behavior and capabilities of GPT-6.2 Astra prior to its release.

item.title: Microsoft unveils six AI models including MAI Code 2 and Flash
item.description: Microsoft unveiled six AI models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, and voice, including the release of MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash on GitHub Copilot. The new models claim high performance at a lower price point compared to competing architectures. This release highlights Microsoft's strategy of building homegrown AI models to control cost structures and challenge third-party providers.

item.title: Microsoft and Salesforce announce Copilotforce partnership
item.description: Microsoft and Salesforce announced Copilotforce, a partnership that integrates Salesforce customer context and actions into Microsoft AI tools like Copilot, Teams, and Fabric. The announcement was made on November 17, 2026. This partnership connects CRM data directly with enterprise productivity and AI platforms, allowing businesses to use customer insights inside tools like Microsoft Copilot.

item.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for ChatGPT Work and Codex
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API with improvements in professional outputs, coding, and efficiency. Astra's standard input and output prices are 20 percent lower than the previous version, while Sol offers lower-cost everyday performance. The release updates OpenAI's frontier and everyday models with lower costs and higher efficiency across multiple platforms and subscription tiers.

item.title: Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore unit revenue in 2025 as it hit $104B
item.description: Nvidia stopped reporting revenue from its Singapore unit in 2025 after the unit's revenue rose 72% year-over-year to $104 billion, accounting for nearly 50% of global revenue. The chipmaker altered its reporting methods as revenues booked through the city-state surged. The shift in Nvidia's financial reporting provides insight into how the company accounts for major regional revenues amidst scrutiny over client relationships and export controls.

item.title: AI models tricked into targeting civilians in simulated military tests
item.description: Independent research by Vals found that leading AI models from companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google can be easily manipulated into identifying civilians, schools, and surrendering soldiers as military targets by framing the scenarios as a game. Models from Anthropic performed the worst in the tests, while OpenAI models performed among the best but still made errors. The findings highlight significant vulnerabilities in current AI safety guardrails regarding autonomous warfare and military target identification.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to testify before US House committees on Dec 1
item.description: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select Committees on Dec 1. The hearing follows his resignation amid a scandal involving an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The testimony could shape U.S. policy on AI chip exports and national‑security oversight of leading semiconductor firms.

item.title: Perplexity CEO says company may launch IPO as early as Q1 2027
item.description: Perplexity accelerated its proposed IPO timeline to as early as the first quarter of 2027 after its annual recurring revenue crossed $1 billion. CEO Aravind Srinivas said faster-than-expected business growth drove the decision to fast-track the listing. The decision places Perplexity on a path to join other major AI firms like OpenAI and Anthropic in the public markets.

item.title: AI in gaming: experts warn against single-field narrative
item.description: Ethan Mollick posted on Bluesky that the narrative that games will be the only field where humans write code unassisted is wrong. He argues that this push from press and fans misses an opportunity to guide AI usage to empower workers and help gaming thrive. It highlights the risk of limiting AI adoption in gaming to a narrow role and the need for broader, worker‑empowering approaches.

item.title: Baidu and Xiaomi CEOs warn of growing gap between AI hype and returns
item.description: Baidu and Xiaomi chief executive officers warned of a growing gap between artificial intelligence hype and financial returns. The remarks highlight executive concerns over commercial outcomes in the sector. Warnings from major technology executives highlight industry caution regarding the commercial viability and financial returns of artificial intelligence investments.

item.title: Genesis AI raises $500 million Series A at $3.5 billion valuation
item.description: Genesis AI, a Paris‑based robot maker, announced a $500 million Series A round valuing the company at $3.5 billion. The funding will support expanding computing infrastructure, robot production and hiring. The round shows strong investor confidence in robots that learn from human motion, indicating a shift toward more capable automation for warehouses, labs and homes.

item.title: Nvidia unveils Nemotron for Science model and Rubin HPC GPU with 50,000+ CUDA cores at SC26
item.description: At the SC26 supercomputing conference, Nvidia announced the Nemotron for Science open model and the Rubin HPC GPU featuring more than 50,000 CUDA cores. The announcements also included new AI‑agent tools, an expanded Vera CPU platform and a collaboration with IBM on quantum computing. The new model and high‑core GPU aim to accelerate AI‑driven scientific simulations, making large‑scale experiments faster and more accessible.

item.title: Stored AI user preferences can silently remove decision-critical details
item.description: A research paper by Joshua Adrian Cahyono examines how AI memory of stored user preferences causes models to silently omit decision-critical information. Testing five models across 100 everyday decision scenarios, the study found that certain models saved brevity preferences and missed critical items in the majority of their later answers. As people increasingly rely on AI assistants for high-stakes decisions in health, finance, and law, automated memory features that silently filter out critical warnings or facts pose a hidden risk to users who never see the omitted information.
